company overview:
Olectra Greentech Limited (Hyderabad, incorporated 2000) is one of India's largest manufacturers of electric buses and a maker of composite/silicone polymer insulators. It completed homologation of its first E-Bus in 2017 and has 8+ years of e-bus manufacturing/commercialisation experience. Two reporting segments:
- **E-vehicle division** — electric buses (7m V2, 9m iX, 12m X2, Coach CX2) and electric tippers; the dominant revenue contributor.
- **Insulator division** — silicone/composite polymer insulators (higher-margin niche).

Scale markers (per deck): Market cap ~INR 102.3 bn (~USD 1.2 bn); 2,700+ EVs on Indian roads; 40+ crore (400M+) clean km; 135+ product variants; 1,000+ employees. Manufacturing at a greenfield Hyderabad plant on 150 acres acquired from TSIIC, with initial capacity 5,000 EVs/year scalable to 10,000 EVs/year.
financial health & performance:
**FY25 (consolidated, audited — from investor presentation):**
- Revenue from operations: **INR 1,80,190 lakh (~INR 1,802 cr)**, up ~56% YoY (FY24: 1,15,414 lakh).
- Adjusted EBITDA: **INR 27,632 lakh (~INR 276 cr)**, up ~49% (FY24: 18,551 lakh); EBITDA margin ~15.3% (consolidated adj.).
- PBT: INR 18,788 lakh, up ~78%; PAT: **INR 13,921 lakh (~INR 139 cr)**, up ~77% (FY24: 7,865 lakh); PAT margin ~7.7%.
- ROCE ~19.2% (FY25). Revenue CAGR FY22–FY25 ~45%; Adj. EBITDA CAGR ~106%; PAT CAGR ~58%.
- EVs sold FY25: 972 (FY24: 541).

**Segment split FY25 (12M):** E-vehicle division revenue INR 1,62,179 lakh (+60.4%), EBITDA INR 22,610 lakh (margin ~13.9%); Insulator division revenue INR 18,011 lakh (+26.0%), EBITDA INR 5,022 lakh (margin ~27.9% — the higher-margin business). Q4FY25 revenue jumped sharply (consolidated Q4 ~INR 44,892 lakh vs Q4FY24 ~28,881 lakh).

**Balance sheet (31-Mar-25, consolidated):** Total assets INR 2,17,140 lakh; Total equity INR 1,05,272 lakh. Borrowings: long-term INR 14,170 lakh (up sharply from ~918 lakh FY24, financing greenfield capex), short-term INR 11,315 lakh. Trade receivables INR 69,352 lakh (up from 51,322 — stretched, working-capital intensive). Inventories INR 28,996 lakh. CWIP INR 18,686 lakh (new plant). Cash & equivalents only INR 567 lakh plus INR 16,462 lakh other bank balances. FY25 net long-term borrowing inflow INR 13,252 lakh funded INR 17,698 lakh of PP&E/intangible capex.

**9MFY26 (per credit rating commentary):** Strong revenue growth and sustained EBITDA margins, driven by a healthy order book — the explicit basis for the rating upgrade. (No standalone 9MFY26 numbers disclosed in either source.)
e-bus delivery / order-book guidance:
- Order book **10,000+ e-buses** (deck). Cumulative orders received: cumulative grew from 90 (FY18) to a single large award of **5,150 buses** ("world's largest e-Bus order") and a peak annual order intake of 8,232 buses (FY24 bar).
- Milestones achieved: 100, 500, then 1,000 buses delivery milestones crossed; first OEM to deliver 500+ e-buses; first E-Tipper delivered.
- Capacity ramp (Hyderabad greenfield): 5,000 → 10,000 EVs/year supports delivery acceleration against the order book.
order book / tenders: Order book 10,000+ e-buses, anchored on **State Transport Undertaking (STU) tenders**. Active fleets across STUs/municipal bodies: PMPML (Pune), TGSRTC (Telangana), HRTC (Himachal), KSRTC (Kerala & Karnataka), GSRTC (Gujarat), BEST (Mumbai), MSRTC (Maharashtra), APSRTC (Andhra), NMC (Nagpur), SMC (Surat), KTCL (Goa), DSCL (Dehradun), SSCL (Silvassa), TTD (Tirumala), TMTU (Thane). Large 5,150-bus award noted as the world's largest single e-bus order.
products / portfolio: E-Bus range: V2 (7m, ~150 km), iX (9m, 180–200 km), X2 (12m, 200–300 km), CX2 Coach (~350 km); plus electric Tipper (launched 2022). Insulator division: silicone/composite polymer insulators. Expansion into electric tippers and broader EV-ecosystem/adjacent segments.
capacity / capex: Greenfield Hyderabad EV plant on 150 acres (acquired from TSIIC); initial capacity 5,000 EVs/yr scalable to 10,000 EVs/yr; operations commenced (partial) for buses and other EV products. CWIP INR 18,686 lakh at FY25-end; FY25 capex ~INR 17,698 lakh, debt-funded.
strategy / roadmap:
- Strengthen inter-city / inter-state private transport segment.
- Entry into staff/private transport segment.
- Expand product line within e-mobility (e.g., electric tippers, coaches).
- Expand into adjacent EV-ecosystem markets and new geographies; continued R&D emphasis.
management / governance: Mgmt details n/a from these sources. Company Secretary: P. Hanuman Prasad (signs filings). Deck cites "professional management and experienced leadership team" as an investment theme. CIN L34100TG2000PLC035451.
industry / demand drivers: EV / e-mobility transition in public transport; government push for electrification of STU fleets; FAME-type / state EV procurement programs; clean-km / emission-reduction mandates. Composite insulators tied to power-T&D capex.
risks / concerns:
- **Customer concentration & payment security:** Heavy reliance on government STUs; payment cycles tied to state finances → stretched receivables (FY25 trade receivables INR 69,352 lakh, up ~35% YoY) and high working-capital intensity.
- **Delivery / execution risk:** Large order book (10,000+) requires capacity ramp; execution and supply-chain (battery/cells) dependence.
- **Leverage rising:** Long-term borrowings stepped up to INR 14,170 lakh (FY25) to fund capex; low cash buffer (INR 567 lakh).
- **Technology/licence dependence:** Historic BYD technology association; competitive intensity in e-bus tenders (Tata, JBM, Switch).
- **Contingent liabilities / performance guarantees** typical of large STU tender contracts (not quantified in these sources).
subsidiaries / associates / entities: Evey Trans (e-bus operating/leasing vehicle) and BYD technology-licence association referenced for Olectra's e-bus platform. Share of profit from associates positive in FY25 (INR 339 lakh).
esg / sustainability: Core business is decarbonising public transport: 2,700+ EVs on road, 40+ crore clean km logged, displacing diesel bus emissions. Electric tippers extend EV into commercial mobility.
other / notes: (Empty — no concall Q&A or additional management commentary available.)
credit rating & financial health:
- **Agency:** India Ratings & Research Private Limited (Ind-Ra).
- **Rating:** **IND A / Stable** (long-term) and **IND A1** (short-term).
- **Rated limits:** Bank loan facilities INR 15,320 million (~INR 1,532 cr).
- **Rating date:** Letter dated **22-May-2026** (intimated to exchanges same day).
- **Rating action:** **UPGRADE** (Ind-Ra upgraded the rating to IND A/Stable/IND A1).
- **Key rationale:** Improved business risk profile supported by a **healthy order book**, which has driven strong revenue growth and **sustained EBITDA margins in 9MFY26**.
- **Leverage / liquidity:** FY25 long-term borrowings INR 14,170 lakh + short-term INR 11,315 lakh against equity INR 1,05,272 lakh (modest gearing). Liquidity supported by INR 16,462 lakh other bank balances though cash & equivalents thin at INR 567 lakh.
- **Concerns:** Stretched trade receivables (INR 69,352 lakh, FY25) and high working-capital intensity given STU exposure; rising debt to fund greenfield capacity; performance-guarantee / contingent-liability exposure typical of government tender execution.

themes.title: EV-OEM & domestic cell manufacturing
themes.need: Domestic EV OEMs and cell/Gigafactory localization (PLI) are scaling unit volumes and chasing battery cost-downs to reach profitability. The binding question is cell-to-pack localization and vehicle-volume ramp, distinct from Tier-1 component supply.
themes.driver: Vehicle-volume ramp + Gigafactory/PLI cell localization & improving EV-OEM unit economics.
